authority: Do not use prior chat context as project state. Load the applicable skills and query the live MCP; checkpoints are only compact navigation caches and must not override MCP state.
validation_checklist_prompt: Before and after every run, execute every item in VALIDATION_CHECKLIST_PROMPT.md. Do not generate until section A passes. Do not approve until section B passes. A first detected defect never ends the audit.
range: When asked to Auto Pilot from a named segment, begin at that exact segment and continue sequentially through the final segment.
autopilot_persistence: While sequential autopilot is active, never treat a user correction, question, commentary exchange, failed take, or checkpoint update as the end of the generation task. Apply the correction, update the durable gate or Bible when relevant, return immediately to the active segment, and continue the Draft-to-Production loop through the final segment unless the user explicitly says stop or a real infrastructure/authority blocker makes further progress impossible.
loop: For each segment: resolve the exact active scene and clip via MCP; pass the asset-integrity gate; audit the complete compiled prompt against Director intent, shot order, and every intended shot beat; fix all confirmed prompt or attachment issues before spending a run; generate Draft-Anime; validate; correct confirmed failures; repeat both the asset-integrity and Director-intent prompt gates; generate Production-Anime; validate; checkpoint; then advance.
asset_integrity_gate: Before every generation request, query the live exact clip and exact segment. Verify active scene UUID and clip ownership; required-assets list; H3 subject bindings; picture labels; authored prompt source; non-stale storyboard path; and successful MCP retrieval/decoding of that exact segment storyboard. Scene-level sheets/panels may be empty for one-image-per-segment packages, but the segment attachment itself must decode. Do not queue while any required asset is missing, substituted, misbound, unreadable, stale, or routed to an inactive duplicate.
per_frame_population_and_identity_gate: HARD GATE before acceptance. Derive the exact allowed human, creature, Beyblade, launcher and stadium count for every shot from the Director plan. At minimum review the full clip at 2 fps, and additionally review every cut neighborhood and any ambiguous motion at 8 fps or higher using full-resolution individual frames, not contact sheets alone. In every sampled frame count complete and partial bodies, faces, heads, hands and silhouettes and confirm each belongs to one continuous declared subject. Reject any clone, duplicate identity, double exposure, transitional ghost, extra partial body, repeated face, mirror/reflection copy, merged identity or unlisted subject unless that duplicate/reflection is explicitly authored. A correct action performed by two copies of the same character is an automatic failure regardless of the 95 percent score.
complete_defect_inventory_gate: A confirmed failure does not end validation. Before changing a prompt, storyboard, asset, or retrying, finish the full-clip audit and record every observable issue across Director beats, framing, composition, population, identity, anatomy, wardrobe, object count, asset fidelity, camera and edit behavior, temporal stability, Beyblade causality and support geometry, dialogue, speaker-mouth routing, extra speech, sound intent, and visual style. Fix the complete evidence-backed issue set together so one retry is not wasted on only the first defect.
offscreen_speaker_visibility_fallback: If a generated take makes a visible silent character mouth an off-screen speaker's line, reject it. Before retrying, preserve the Director action but reframe the visible non-speaker to a back or three-quarter-away angle, or otherwise keep that non-speaker's mouth outside the composition, while retaining required identity, anatomy and population. The authored off-screen speaker remains unseen and is the only voice.
storyboard_recreation_authority: The agent is authorized to recreate a current segment storyboard when the attached storyboard conflicts with corrected canon, physics, wardrobe, anatomy, blocking, prop coverage, camera intent, or repeatedly causes model grounding failures. Every recreation must be generated fresh from the original Director source asset sheets and current authoritative beat specification. Never use, edit, trace, recolor, composite, or recursively regenerate from an earlier storyboard or rejected output, because stacked pixels cause color, identity, geometry, and composition drift. Preserve the Director's valid shot beats and timing while correcting the faulty visual instruction. Before the next generation, attach the replacement to the exact segment, verify it decodes and is non-stale, re-read the complete compiled prompt, and repeat every asset, appearance, physics, dialogue, and Director-intent gate.
subject_appearance_gate: Before every generation, enumerate each visible subject's canonical physical traits and exact wardrobe for every shot, plus each adjacent prop or covering as a separate object. Reject any prompt or take where clothing changes category, length, color, pattern, or identity; where shorts become trousers; where bedding becomes clothing or a limb; where a covering object is substituted; or where a subject, garment, blanket, limb, or prop merges or morphs into another. For SEG_SC002_004 specifically, Kaiden remains in cobalt-blue T-shirt and black athletic shorts with white side stripes, and the Beyblade begins fully covered by the separate blue-grey bed blanket—not trousers—until Kaiden lifts the blanket corner.
beyblade_physics_bible: Whenever a segment contains a Beyblade, launcher, ripcord, stadium, collision, knockout, spin-state change, damage state, or Bit Beast, read BEYBLADE_PHYSICS_BIBLE.md before directing or generating and apply every relevant rule as a hard validation gate. Never reinvent, infer, substitute, or improvise Beyblade physics outside the Bible; add a reviewed rule to the Bible first if a required mechanic is absent.
spin_causality_gate: A Beyblade may begin spinning only from visible physical input: a hand deliberately spins it, a correctly attached launcher and ripcord or winder releases it, or the take begins with continuous carry-over from the immediately previous authored shot where it was already spinning. No physical, dream, symbolic, magical, or Bit Beast beat may make a stationary Beyblade self-start. Reject any unexplained orientation change, circular trail, spin blur, or sudden RPM as self-start. A camera orbit or roll also fails whenever it creates ambiguous apparent axial rotation; for a stationary symbolic top, lock both top and camera and use only non-circular lighting or background motion.
director_intent_prompt_gate: Before every generation, read the exact current segment Director record and complete compiled prompt. Confirm that assets, identities, blocking, camera, timing, dialogue or silence, sound intent, causal order, transitions, and every Director shot beat agree. If any part is missing, contradictory, ambiguous, or likely to waste the run, correct and re-read the prompt before generating.
camera_direction_gate: Before every generation, enumerate the permitted camera movement, speed, duration, lens behavior, screen direction, and transition for every shot using the Director's camera/edit intent. Do not introduce a movement merely to add energy. Reject or rewrite any unspecified, unmotivated, unusable, contradictory, or overly fast zoom, push, dolly, orbit, roll, whip, speed ramp, interpolation, or focal-length change. A hard cut must remain instantaneous with no generated travel between panels. A pan must preserve camera distance and focal length, move at the authored pace, maintain screen direction, and never masquerade as a zoom. After generation, any camera movement outside that per-shot allowlist is a hard failure even when the scene otherwise matches 95 percent. CAMERA FALLBACK: if a generated allowed pan is rendered as an unapproved zoom, push or scale change, do not retry the same ambiguous motion. Replace it with locked usable coverage that preserves the Director's subject priority and screen direction, then re-run preflight.
physical_staging_gate: Before every generation, classify each Beyblade appearance as physical action, stable supported handling, stopped/resting, or explicitly symbolic/non-physical imagery. A physical Beyblade may spin only after a Bible-valid launcher release or when already spinning on a valid continuous surface; it must never spin freely in a palm, fingers, pocket, bedding, or unsupported air. A stopped top must have readable gravity/contact support and may not hover or balance upright on its tip. Any circular trail, ring, blur, aura, or changing orientation around a top reads as rotation and fails unless that rotation is explicitly Bible-valid. Symbolic rotation must be isolated from hands, bodies, launchers, and real-world surfaces so it cannot be read as physical mechanics. Also require every visible person to have the correct count of complete, distinct, anatomically readable limbs, including two separate legs when both should be visible. Any ambiguity fails preflight and must be rewritten before generation.
generation_preset_directive: Before every generation preset choice, call list_h3_presets, choose only an id returned there, and call get_h3_preset on that exact id. A listed id that returns 404 is unusable and must not be passed to generation. Pass an exact successfully resolved preset_id for a one-shot run, or omit preset_id only when intentionally using the film's saved h3_settings unchanged. Never invent preset ids or individual Comfy/H3 knobs such as steps, megapixels, turbo, LoRA, sampler, or scheduler. quality and update_movie_quality are labels only and never select generation knobs.
production_settings_gate: Never queue Production until the exact new Draft covers every Director beat, reaches at least 95 percent scene adherence, and passes every applicable validation and hard gate. Then repeat the asset-integrity and Director-intent prompt gates, resolve the intended Production preset through list_h3_presets plus successful get_h3_preset, and pass that exact usable preset_id. If intentionally using the film's saved h3_settings, omit preset_id; quality remains label-only.
temporary_draft_only_mode: ACTIVE until the user explicitly says otherwise. Generate and validate only Draft quality for each segment. After a Draft passes every applicable Director, asset, appearance, camera, temporal, audio and Physics Bible gate, checkpoint it as Draft-accepted and advance directly to the next segment. Do not queue, retry, or imply authorization for Production while this mode is active.
acceptance: After generation, proceed only when every Director shot beat is covered, overall scene adherence is at least 95 percent, and every validator and hard gate passes. Any missing primary beat or failed validator rejects the take. Beyblade Physics Bible failures can never be excused by the scene score.
temporal_validation: For every completed take, inspect at least two evenly spaced frames per second across the full duration (minimum 30 frames for 15 seconds), with additional attention immediately before and after every authored cut. Fail on visible frame jitter, malformed or duplicated cut frames, identity drift, missing, merged, duplicated or malformed limbs, prop or population popping, geometry discontinuity, unintended split-screen or board leakage, dialogue-mouth routing errors, or any Physics Bible discontinuity.
audio_validation: For every completed take, audit the full audio track against the exact Director dialogue and sound intent. Every scripted line must be present once, spoken only by its assigned speaker, with matching visible lip movement when that speaker is on screen. Reject missing, duplicated, reassigned, paraphrased, or extra dialogue; reject speech in silence or ambience-only beats; and reject any visible non-speaker lip-syncing another voice.
media_preview: When a generation finishes successfully, download the exact newly versioned video for the exact active clip through MCP and embed the local video in chat instead of showing a latent image. Never substitute an older take. If a run is stopped or fails before creating a new take, state that no new video exists and do not show the old clip as its result.
review_authority: The user delegates final readiness decisions to the agent. Exact downloaded video is for user preview and does not block approval or advancement. Judge the exact new take from the strongest MCP evidence available; rerun when scene match or a hard physics gate fails, otherwise approve and continue.
safety: Never generate against inactive duplicates. Require a newly versioned exact-clip path before reviewing. Stop only for a real blocker, required authority, or repeated infrastructure failure.
